llm_recommendations.reason_for_recommendation: Q2 earnings beat estimates (constant-currency revenue growth of 2.7% vs est 1-1.2%, EBIT margin improved to 16.3% vs est 16%, PAT increased 53.7%), supported by one-time gain from divesting SWC business. AI-related contracts accounted for 50% of total contract value. Reiterated 5-year revenue growth aspiration (13-15%) and margins (16-17%). Board approved interim dividend of ₹20 per share. Brokerages upgraded ratings and raised target prices (IDBI Capital upgraded to 'buy' from 'hold' and raised target to ₹4,170 from ₹3,625).

Upcoming initial public offering (IPO), expected to be India's biggest ever. Company's growth plans extend beyond telecom, focusing on digital services, AI, and cloud ambitions, along with satellite connectivity and 6G technology.

Announces worldwide job cuts from November to establish a 'stronger performance culture' and address underperformance. Faces pressure from weakening demand for electronic products and soaring memory prices. Projected quarterly profit below analysts' estimates and warned of faster decline in Apple-related business. Diversifying revenue beyond smartphones into high-growth markets like AI-powered data centers and connected-device technologies, expecting most chip revenue from non-handset businesses by FY27. Shares fell 1.16% in pre-market trading.
Gautam Adani (chairman of Adani Group) scheduled to meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio for India-US economic discussions, indicating potential strategic alignment or deals.
N Chandrasekaran (Tata Group chief) scheduled to meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio for India-US economic discussions, indicating potential strategic alignment or deals.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visiting Reliance Industries in Jamnagar for India-US economic discussions, indicating potential strategic alignment or deals.

Initial Public Offering (IPO) opened, expected to be India's largest-ever. Strong interest with Grey Market Premium (GMP) of Rs 245 (suggesting potential listing price of Rs 1,364, 22% above upper issue price). Strong financial performance (FY26 revenue Rs 1.46 lakh crore, net profit Rs 30,049 crore) and robust subscriber base (533.3 million). Anchor investors include LIC, BlackRock. Proceeds to be used for debt repayment. Brokerages recommend subscribing for potential listing gains and long-term growth (5G, broadband, AI, cloud computing).

Reported job cuts across its global workforce from November, described as a 'performance-focused reduction'. Weak handset demand has hurt the company, with stock gaining only 1.5% in 2026 compared to S&P 500's 12% and Philadelphia Semiconductor Index's nearly 60% rise. Diversifying revenue beyond smartphones is a key strategy.
